newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Some voting allowed after polls close in Gambia.
newsitem.headline: Some voting allowed after polls close in Gambia.

text.p: Electoral officials in Gambia ordered polling stations to stay open to allow people in queues to vote in the West African country's civilian-rule presidential elections.
Officials of the Provisional Independent Electoral Commission said many people had still not voted at the official close of polls at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT).
"They will continue to vote as long as there are people in the queue. That's what is allowed under the law," a spokeswoman said.
Commission officials expected the final turnout to top the 87 percent scored in last month's national referendum on a new constitution.
Military leader Yahya Jammeh, who seized power in a 1994 coup, faced three civilian challengers with lawyer Ousainou Darboe likely to emerge as the strongest contender.
First results were expected late on Thursday nigt with the winner likely to be known late on Friday, officials said.
